tier_reason: Upgraded from C. The README tables come from the public Google Benchmark targets (demo1_bench and the FFTW bench, built with Bazel --config=opt from src/.bazelrc). The repo's report/report.pdf (section 4.1, same parameters as the README) names the CPU (Intel i7-6700K 4 GHz, scaling off, single core), the compiler (gcc) and flags for MPSFT and for the locally built FFTW 3.3.6-pl2. The gcc version is not stated.

corrections.claimed_speedup: At N=4194301 (prime near 2^22) MPSFT takes 19.4 ms at S=64, 75.8 ms at S=512, 140.8 ms at S=1024 and 263.4 ms at S=2048; FFTW at N=4194304 takes 225.3 ms with FFTW_ESTIMATE (benchmark arg 64) and 102.3 ms with FFTW_MEASURE (arg 0). The README and report say it is faster than FFTW when S is below about 1800, which is the FFTW_ESTIMATE crossover; the README also says S must be around 1000 to beat FFTW, matching FFTW_MEASURE. Derived from page data: 5.3x faster than FFTW_MEASURE and 11.6x faster than FFTW_ESTIMATE at S=64; break-even against FFTW_MEASURE between S=512 and S=1024.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: gcc (version not stated; the report discusses gcc autovectorization and .bazelrc uses the GCC-only -fopt-info-vec-optimized), Bazel --config=opt: -std=c++11 -O3 -ffast-math -mavx2 -mtune=native -fopenmp-simd -g0 -DNDEBUG; FFTW 3.3.6-pl2 compiled locally with -O3 -mtune=native -ffast-math (report section 4.1); CPU scaling disabled; single-threaded.
corrections.caveats: Wins hold only for sparse spectra (S below about 1000 against FFTW_MEASURE). MPSFT is timed at prime N=4194301 while FFTW runs at the power of two 4194304, FFTW's best case. The report says MPSFT is not competitive with sFFT1 or sFFT2 at N near 2^22 (they win there; MPSFT only overtakes them at larger N with S=50). The input model is a noisy sparse spectrum (sigma=0.1), and MPSFT returns approximate modes, not an exact DFT. The report is explicitly 'not a formal publication'. GPL-2.0 text is in src/COPYING.txt; whether 'or later' applies is not stated. The README says it plans to drop the FFTW dependency (KissFFT), which never happened. Last commit 2017.

notes: Numbers verified; the FFTW block mapping is confirmed by FFTW's flag values (FFTW_ESTIMATE = 64, FFTW_MEASURE = 0 in the benchmark names). The report PDF in the repo supplies the CPU and flags, so I upgraded C to A. The '1800' headline is against FFTW_ESTIMATE only.

tier_reason: doc/OfftSpeedComparison.md is a first-party table against FFTW 3.3.5 (FFTW_ESTIMATE, with and without SIMD) and oneMKL, with compiler (MSYS2 GCC 12.2.0) and CPU (i5-2450M). Optimization flags are not stated, and CMakeLists.txt sets only warnings and -std=c++11, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Author: for arbitrary sizes OFFT is often faster than FFTW, even the SIMD version. From the table (ns per n ln n): OFFT beats FFTW_ESTIMATE with SIMD at 10 of 30 non-power-of-two lengths (e.g. 1025: 6.7 vs 8.0; 4097: 6.0 vs 7.4; 262145: 9.0 vs 11.6; 16777217: 8.7 vs 12.3, i.e. 1.41x derived from page data), ties at 4194305, and loses at the other 19. It beats single-thread MKL at 12 of 30 non-power-of-two lengths (e.g. 32769: 7.2 vs 14.4; 4194305: 9.7 vs 14.7) and 2-thread MKL at 3 (2047, 65537, 131073). It is slower than FFTW with SIMD and than MKL at every power of two and ten (1024: 2.1 vs 0.5).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: GCC 12.2.0 (MSYS2 Rev11) on Windows; optimization flags not stated (CMakeLists.txt sets only -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -std=c++11; build type not given). FFTW 3.3.5 official Windows DLLs; MKL vendor binaries.
corrections.caveats: Mixed result that the author's wording overstates: slower than FFTW_ESTIMATE with SIMD at powers of two and ten and at 19 of 30 non-power-of-two sizes (one tie); slower than MKL at all regular sizes, but faster than single-thread MKL at 12 awkward sizes. FFTW_MEASURE was deliberately not used. Old CPU (SSE4 only), no SIMD in OFFT, optimization flags not stated, FFTW 3.3.5 Windows binaries. The author says the numbers are noisy (background processes, thermal clock changes).

notes: Win counts recomputed from the table; the record's 'slower than MKL' was too broad (OFFT beats 1-core MKL at 12 of 30 awkward sizes). BSL-1.0, 3 stars, last commit 2024-05-12 (main), stale, all confirmed.
